source.title: Regularization Matters: A Nonparametric Perspective on Overparametrized Neural Network
source.authors: Wen-Jia Wang; Tianyang Hu; Cong Lin; Guang Cheng

page_placements.theme: Regularization and capacity controls have setting-dependent effects

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplementary material, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests overparameterized networks trained on noisy data and reports that unregularized networks overfit; its MNIST experiments add Gaussian noise to labels rather than randomizing them, and its claims concern noisy regression and estimation error.
record.gate_note: The paper does not report experiments fitting completely random labels, shuffled pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs. It discusses earlier random-label work only as cited prior work. Its own experiments add Gaussian noise to real labels and measure test misclassification or L2 estimation error, not training error on fully random labels; the theoretical results address noisy regression. Those results bear on regularization and noisy-label learning but do not test most claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures recovery of a regression function and clean-test classification under additive Gaussian target noise. It does not establish any claim version: training fit on randomized class labels, convergence comparisons, input randomization, or separate learning of signal and noise. Its regularization results concern noisy targets rather than V5's random-label fitting and generalization on true labels. T5 is therefore unwarranted.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. More precisely, under the stated assumptions, unregularized one-hidden-layer ReLU networks have L2 estimation error bounded away from zero when trained too briefly or too long. Suitable L2-regularized GD achieves a minimax-optimal estimation rate. Experiments support improved function recovery and robustness under additive Gaussian target noise.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies theoretical GD on one-hidden-layer ReLU networks and experiments with two-hidden-layer ReLU networks trained by RMSProp, comparing additive Gaussian label noise and L2 regularization. It does not apply the original fully randomized-label intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different qualitative outcomes by noise standard deviation and by regularization: ONN test misclassification increases with additive noise, while ONN+L2 is described as lower and more stable. It also notes NTK+ES performs worst when σ ≤ 0.5 and better than NTK and ONN when σ ≥ 1 on MNIST.

fits_no_version.finding: MNIST test misclassification increases with additive Gaussian target noise; L2-regularized networks perform better and more consistently.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-validated L2 regularization improves clean-test classification under additive Gaussian target noise in the tested networks.

fits_no_version.finding: At sigma=1, unregularized ONN test misclassification rises late in training while ONN+L2 remains stable through 50K iterations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: L2 regularization reduces late-training overfitting under additive target noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Unregularized networks recover the simulated target functions poorly, while ONN+L2 performs best, including when the target function is zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: L2 regularization improves function recovery from Gaussian-noise regression observations in these simulations.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 4.1 and 5.2 establish nonvanishing estimation error for unregularized GD at specified short or long training durations and an optimal convergence rate with suitable L2 regularization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated NTK and nonparametric assumptions, suitable L2 regularization enables consistent function estimation from noisy observations.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2021; PMLR Volume 130)
record.problems: The empirical neural-network experiments use RMSProp rather than the GD analyzed theoretically. The experiments add Gaussian noise to labels instead of replacing labels with fully random labels. The main result plots provide qualitative descriptions but the supplied text does not give numeric plotted values. The MNIST experiment measures test misclassification, not L2 estimation error.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training error and chance test error on completely randomized class labels using unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time for real and random labels, and convergence as the corrupted-label fraction increases.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and test error approaching chance across a sweep of randomized-label fractions.
Random-label fitting despite weight decay, dropout or augmentation; generalization on true labels after removing these regularizers.
Separate measurement of real-pattern learning before noisy-label memorization.

record.verdict_notes: The zero-function simulation uses wholly random Gaussian targets, so the record's broad suggestion that every experiment adds noise to real labels needs qualification. It still supplies no measured random-class-label interpolation result. Missing numeric plot values do not turn these related outcomes into tests of the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment trains on completely randomized labels or reports training error and test error at chance.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed for true versus random labels.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment.
Experiments add Gaussian noise to labels; they do not sweep the fraction of randomly corrupted labels or measure perfect training fit and test error toward chance.

The paper tests L2 regularization on additive-noise labels, but does not test random-label fitting, dropout, data augmentation, or whether removing regularization alone harms generalization on true labels.
No learning-order or real-versus-random-label memorization analysis.

rows.subject: ONN

rows.operation_detail: Compared test misclassification rate across additive Gaussian label-noise standard deviations on MNIST digits 5 vs. 8.

rows.value: As σ increases, all misclassification rates increase; ONN performs worse than ONN+L2, whose misclassification rate is smaller and more stable.

rows.value: ONN+L2 performs significantly better than ONN with smaller misclassification rate and better stability; numeric values not stated in text.
